page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with no margin notes. The running head is at the top, and the page number 106 is printed at the top left. A catchword ("Assyriorum") stands at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: deinde fœlices successus & uictorias, suæ industriæ, sapientiæ, potentiæ acceptas fert. Qui sane fines quandoquidem mali sunt, ac meæ gloriæ aduersantur, præbent mihi causam, ut ipsum quoq; iustè perdam. Egregia igitur doctrina nobis hic proposita est de prouidentia Dei, per quam omnia quidè quæ in mundo sunt aut fiunt, ordinantur ac disponuntur, atq; inter cætera etiam ad malas actiones homines inducitur, quādo uidelicet uti ijs Deus decernit tanquam instrumentis ad exequendum iustitiæ & potentiæ suæ opera. Atqui dum ij alio fine atq; alio animo agunt omnia quàm Deus constituit, fit ut causa mali penes ipsos homines resideat, Deo autē imputari malum nullo modo possit. Aptè uerò propheta per mimesin recitat uerba Regum Assyriorum, sibi suisq; uiribus victorias omnes tribuentium, & Deū nequaquam agnoscentium. Qualibus etiam usus legitur crudelis Sennaherib oppugnans Ierusalem, 2.Reg.18. Latentq; in illis uerbis pleraque argumentationes à pari, siue à maiore ad minus, tanquā si diceretur: Ego habeo mihi subditos etiam reges, quorum plurimi soli possent expugnare Regem Iuda: quanto igitur facilius ego tantundem potero? Item: Superaui tot inclytasmu-nitasq; ciuitates, quid 'ni igitur superem et Ierusalem? Carchemis regio ultra Babylonē. Ibidem etiam Calno, de qua Gen.10. Amos 6. Hamath, postea Antiochia dicta. Arpad, Damascus in Syria. Vbi uerò ait: Et erit, cū cōsummauerit, &c. tempus notat quo subuertetur Af-

page.notes: The page is a single column. The printed text is set in roman with italic passages and Greek and Hebrew are absent. The "syriorum" on the last line is the catchword's continuation printed at the right; it is rendered as the catchword and kept out of the main text except as the word completing "Af-". The line-end hyphen in "inclytas-mu-nitasq;" is uncertain and marked by the printed break; "quādo" and "quàdo" are read with a diacritic that may be a tilde or acute. The running head "IESAIAE" is written "JESAIAE" per the consonant-i rule.
